name: divider-ratio-dff
description: setup/hold/clk->Q of dff_tg_3v3, the transmission-gate master-slave flop the divider chain and its retiming flop are built from
claim: #11 (design input, not a spec line) -- what are the setup time, hold time and clk->Q of dff_tg_3v3, the transmission-gate master-slave flop every divider cell and the retiming flop are built from (DR-001 Decision 3: "static CMOS throughout (transmission-gate master-slave flops)")? The setup number is the one DR-001 Decision 3 requires in order to state whether the retiming flop's budget closes at the slow corner; the closure itself is sim/divider-ratio-chain's retiming_margin.csv, joined against this record.
methodology: Setup: 10 copies per bank share one clock; copy i sees its data 50% crossing ti before the clock's 50% crossing, ti = 1.00, 0.20, 0.10, 0.05, 0.02, 0.00, -0.02, -0.05, -0.10, -0.15 ns. Bank A captures 0->1, bank B captures 1->0. Setup time is the smallest ti whose clk->Q has not degraded by more than 10% against the same bank's ti = 1.00 ns reference -- the standard degradation criterion. Each ladder step's clk->Q is a raw_measures trig/targ .measure marked 'optional': a step past the flop's true setup time fails to capture within the td=20ns window, which ngspice reports as a failed .measure -- the harness records that as not-measured data (sim/harness README 'Expected .measure failures') rather than discarding the point, which is exactly what makes the ladder scan (testbench/derive.py, a sim/harness 'derived' measure) able to tell 'violated' from 'not simulated'.

Hold: 10 further copies (bank C) hold data low through the measured edge and transition 0->1 only th afterwards, th = 0.50 ... -0.70 ns. Hold is met at a step if Q stays below 10% of the rail until the next clock edge -- an avg measurement, which cannot fail, so bank C's raw_measures are required rather than optional.

The first clock edge preconditions every flop and the second (25.05 ns) is the one measured, so no result depends on the DC operating point of a bistable latch; every output measurement carries td=20ns for the same reason (see testbench/tb_dff_setup.sp header for the ff/125C failure mode this guards against).
Simulator settings: tran 10p 35n, reltol 1e-3, abstol 1e-10, vntol 1e-5, chgtol 1e-13 -- unchanged from the pre-harness deck.

Limitation -- ladder floor. Where the reported setup equals the last ladder step (-0.15 ns) the criterion was never tripped, so the true setup time is at or below that value and the number is a bound, not a measurement. That is the safe direction for the retiming margin computed downstream only because the bound is pessimistic: a smaller true setup can only increase the margin.
Limitation -- schematic-level. No extracted parasitics; clock and data both driven by ideal 100 ps -edge sources. Post-layout re-extraction is #18's scope and will supersede these numbers.
Statistical switches: sw_stat_global = sw_stat_mismatch = 0 (nominal device skew from the corner section only, no Monte Carlo mismatch).

This record supersedes 20260731-171815-0a12e6c (same claim, same 45-point grid, run through the sim/lib/simenv.sh shim rather than sim/harness) as a tooling migration -- see the Supersedes field for the numeric-agreement check against it.
